notes.text: Overall, the codebase is well-structured for its age and purpose. Core files (application.js, router/index.js, response.js, request.js) are large but internally organized. The main technical debt is file size and duplication (res.sendFile/sendfile). Test files are excessively large and should be modularized. The router's parameter handling has a potential edge case with object/array param values. No critical security issues found in the excerpts. The 'insecure http:// endpoint' finding on lib/response.js:82 is a false positive (regex pattern). The TODO marker in request.js:452 could not be verified. No lockfile check possible without package.json. The test/support/utils.js hub is appropriate for shared test utilities.

findings.title: Oversized response.js (1,179 lines) violates single responsibility
findings.description: response.js contains 1,179 lines handling HTTP response methods (send, json, jsonp, sendFile, download, redirect, format, cookie, header manipulation, ETag, content negotiation, etc.). This violates single responsibility and makes the file hard to maintain.
findings.suggestion: Split into multiple modules: response-core.js (core prototype), response-send.js (send/json/jsonp), response-files.js (sendFile/sendfile/download), response-cookies.js (cookie/clearCookie), response-headers.js (set/get/append/header/links/location/redirect), response-negotiation.js (format/type/vary), response-cache.js (ETag/freshness).
findings.benefit: Improves maintainability, testability, and readability; enables tree-shaking for users who don't need all features.
findings.risk: Medium - requires careful refactoring to preserve public API; all methods are attached to the same prototype object.

findings.title: 20-line block duplicated within response.js

findings.title: Oversized router/index.js (674 lines) with complex routing logic
findings.description: router/index.js contains 674 lines with complex routing logic (handle, process_params, param, use, route, VERB methods, layer matching, parameter merging). The handle function alone is ~200 lines with nested callbacks and state management.
findings.suggestion: Extract layer matching logic (matchLayer, getPathname, getProtohost), parameter processing (process_params, mergeParams), and route dispatch into separate modules. Consider splitting into router-core.js, router-layer.js, router-params.js.
findings.benefit: Reduces cognitive complexity, improves testability of individual routing concerns, makes middleware/parameter handling easier to reason about.
findings.risk: Medium - router is core to Express; changes must preserve exact routing semantics including edge cases with mounted apps, mergeParams, and parameter callbacks.

findings.title: No lockfile committed next to package.json
findings.description: Without a lockfile, every `npm install` resolves fresh versions — CI, teammates, and production can drift apart silently.
findings.suggestion: Commit the lockfile matching your package manager (npm/yarn/pnpm) and install with `npm ci` in CI.
findings.benefit: Identical dependency trees everywhere; fewer "works on my machine" failures.
findings.risk: None — adding a lockfile is additive.

modelVerdicts.reason: Repository-level finding; package.json not in excerpts; cannot verify lockfile presence

findings.title: Potential object reference comparison bug in param callback tracking
findings.description:
In process_params, paramCalled.match === paramVal uses strict equality (===) to detect if a param callback was already invoked with the same value. For objects/arrays (possible with complex route patterns), this compares references not values, potentially causing duplicate callback execution or incorrect caching.

> Validation: cited 200-250 does not contain the snippet — actual lines are 378-393; citation corrected
findings.suggestion: Use a stable serialization (e.g., JSON.stringify) or a Map with value-based keys for paramCalled tracking, or document that param values are always strings/primitives.
findings.benefit: Prevents subtle bugs with complex route parameters (e.g., regex captures returning arrays).
findings.risk: Low - route parameters are typically strings; but regex captures can produce arrays. Changing comparison could affect performance.

findings.title: Inconsistent error handling in res.send for numeric status codes
findings.description: res.send(status) where status is a number sets the status code and sends the status message as plain text body. However, if statuses.message[chunk] is undefined (unknown status code), chunk becomes undefined, leading to empty body with Content-Type text/plain. res.sendStatus handles this by falling back to String(statusCode).
findings.suggestion: Align res.send(status) behavior with res.sendStatus: use `statuses.message[chunk] || String(chunk)` for the body.
findings.benefit: Consistent behavior for unknown status codes; avoids empty response bodies.
findings.risk: Low - only affects deprecated res.send(status) usage; res.sendStatus is the recommended API.
